hypotheses.title: Stage 6 (semantic analysis) validates a module's functions and classes serially, the only per-function stage not parallelised
hypotheses.issue: semantics/internal/analysis/declarations.go: Analyze builds one scope.NewPackage(ctx, semtypes.ContextFrom(env), ...) root context, and validatePackage then runs `for _, fn := range common.DeclaredNodes(pkg.Functions) { validateFunction(cx, fn) }`, and the same serial loop over pkg.ClassDefinitions/validateClass, on a single goroutine. Stages 5, 7, 8 and 10 process function bodies concurrently, so on a 4-core machine stage 6 runs at CPU/wall ~1.0 while stage 5 runs at ~3.7. On large modules stage 6 therefore takes as much wall time as stage 5 (~280 ms each on the 8000-function reproducer) despite doing ~4x less CPU work. Function and class validations are independent: the only mutable state they share is the single semtypes.Context held in scope.packageContext (its subtype-check memo caches); moduleVars is read-only after NewPackage, the CompilerContext lookups used by the analyzer are read-only env lookups that stage 5 already does concurrently, and per-function maps live in per-call contexts. The one ordering concern is diagnostics: CompilerContext.addDiagnostic appends in emission order and nothing downstream sorts them, so concurrent validation must buffer diagnostics per declaration and replay them in declaration order.

reproducer.command:
python3 gen_stage6.py 8000 main.bal  # place in a package dir with Ballerina.toml (stage6pkg/)
./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> stage6pkg/
# per-stage: harness mirroring test_util/testphases.RunPipeline printing wall/CPU per stage on stage6_serial.bal

hypotheses.baseline: main, 4 cores, 8000-function file: stage 6 = 276-300 ms wall, 266-278 ms CPU (x0.9-1.0); stage 5 = 280-315 ms wall, 1040-1230 ms CPU (x3.7-3.9). `bal run` on stage6pkg: 6.17-6.46 s wall, ~2.4 GB max RSS. On corpus/bench/10-bench/expressions-v.bal stage 6 is ~1.1 s wall at CPU/wall ~1.0 (~12% of the frontend).

hypotheses.fix_approach: Replace the serial function and class-definition loops in validatePackage with a generic validateConcurrently helper: min(GOMAXPROCS, n) workers pull indices from an atomic counter; each worker creates its own semtypes.ContextFrom(env) and, per declaration, a scope.Fork(cx, tyCtx) — a shallow copy of the root packageContext sharing moduleVars/compilerCtx but with the worker's type context and a per-declaration diagnostic buffer (packageContext gets a `reports` sink field: the CompilerContext for the root, a reportBuffer for forks). After wg.Wait the buffers are flushed in declaration order so diagnostics are byte-identical to the serial order, and a panic in a worker is recovered per declaration and re-raised on the calling goroutine after flushing earlier diagnostics (projects.runPerModule and test harnesses rely on recover on that goroutine). The serial barriers between declaration kinds (imports/constants/globals/services, then functions, then type defs/annotations/init, then classes) are preserved. Pitfalls: (1) diagnostic ordering is emission-order, not sorted — must buffer and replay; (2) per-worker semtypes.Context means no memo sharing across workers, so total stage-6 CPU roughly doubles (~270 -> ~500 ms) — partly that, partly read-side contention on CompilerEnvironment.symbolSpace's RWMutex, which also limits the gain on lambda-heavy code like expressions-v; the wall win is still ~2x on 4 cores; (3) TraceSpan.StartChild/End are already goroutine-safe. Determinism checked with a 400-error file: identical output 10/10 runs vs main.

notes: Out-of-scope observation from exploration: on corpus/bench/09-bench/huge-project-v all 215 files parse serially (~4.8 s of an 18 s build) because projects.(*documentContext).moduleLoadRequests triggers parsing via sync.Once during import discovery, before parseDocumentsParallel runs. Fix would be in projects/ (out of this routine's scope) but looks worth a look.
